newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher again, led by gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher again, led by gold.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended sharply higher for the second day in a row Friday, led by heavy fund shortcovering in gold, traders said.

"The slump in the stock market Friday might be used as an excuse for gold's recovery, but really it was just that funds are taking the opportunity to cover their large short positions, plus there's been some producers (who) have been lifting hedges this week," Merrill Lynch commodity research director, Bill O'Neill, said.
"However, our view is that this is a natural trading turn in the market, but may not be a major trend change, and the 12 year lows seen last week may yet be revisited," he said.
COMEX August gold ended up $4.90 an ounce at $329.60, after seeing an eleven day high at $330.90 intraday.
COMEX gold total volume was estimated at a heavy 55,000 lots, with traders reporting 3,000 lots of exchange-for-physicals done as well.
The move followed a $6.00 jump in August gold on Thursday.
The August/December spread widened back out to $4.00 an ounce from $3.50 Thursday.
Open interest in COMEX gold fell 3,064 lots Thursday to 219,005 contracts, and traders predicted it would be down sharply in Monday's data on Friday's trading.

COMEX gold open interest saw its highest level in 18 months earlier this week at 222,069 contracts, with net short positions held by funds believed to be at new record levels around 90,000 lots, equivalent to about 300 tonnes of gold.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted around $328.70/20, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $324.20 and the New York close Thursday around $323.50/00.

Gold fixed at a 12 year low last week at $315.75 in London, in the wake of news of a sale of 167 tonnes of gold by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), which encouraged massive amounts of extra short selling by hedge funds, analysts said.

Implied lease rates for gold eased further to around 2.15 percent for one month Friday, from a six month high around 2.60 percent early this week, suggesting hedge fund borrowing demand, to fund short positions, may be easing, traders said.

The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's index of North American mining stocks .XAU also moved higher, up 2.91 percent at 96.91 points near the close, even though the Dow Jones Industrial Index was down more than 130 points near the close.

COMEX September silver ended up 2.5 cent at $4.270 an ounce, recovering from a breakdown to contract lows this week at $414.50. The September/December spread narrowed to 5.0 cents from 6.2 cents Thursday.
In the bullion market, silver fixed at a three year lows at $4.2235 an ounce earlier this week.
But silver has lagged relative to gold this week, with the spot gold/silver ratio climbing to 76.7 at the close -- its highest levels since January.
NYMEX platinum group metal (PGM) futures also ended higher as the white metals continued to recover from two month lows seen in the past week.

NYMEX October platinum closed up $5.60 at $399.30, after climbing back over $400.00 intraday for the first time in two weeks, but October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread was little changed around $69.00 an ounce.
NYMEX September palladium gained $6.00 to end at $166.35.

Russian shipments of palladium to Japan have resumed this week, with the arrival of three tonnes of palladium at Narita Airport in Tokyo, but no platinum arrivals have yet been reported, with Russian officials saying packaging problems are delaying the shipments.
